question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Timed degron depletion: establishment vs. maintenance
ideas.description: Use dTAG/AID-tagged FOS/JUN family members and deplete during the first stimulus only, or only after stimulus withdrawal but before rechallenge. Measuring recall transcription and accessibility distinguishes AP-1 as an initiator from AP-1 as a continuously required maintainer of memory.

ideas.title: Long-chase occupancy and accessibility time course
ideas.description: Perform CUT&RUN for AP-1 subunits and ATAC-seq at multiple times after transient stimulus, extending through many cell divisions. Test whether AP-1-bound, newly opened sites persist after AP-1 levels return to baseline, and whether persistence predicts stronger rechallenge response.

ideas.title: Sufficiency by synthetic AP-1 recruitment
ideas.description: Use optogenetic or chemically induced AP-1 activation, or dCas9-targeted AP-1 domains, at specific loci in naive cells with a pulse and then withdrawal. If the locus retains accessibility and shows primed re-induction without the native stimulus, AP-1 is sufficient for memory.

ideas.title: Motif-level necessity at memory enhancers
ideas.description: Use base editing or CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs at selected memory-associated enhancers, then run a stimulus-rest-rechallenge paradigm. Compare chromatin marks and gene induction with unedited controls and with edits to neighboring non-AP-1 motifs to establish cis-level necessity.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-resolved memory and mitotic bookmarking
ideas.description: Combine live-cell FOS/JUN reporters or barcoded lineage tracing with single-cell multiome readouts, and image or profile AP-1 on mitotic chromatin. Test whether sister cells share memory states and AP-1 occupancy, and whether blocking division or bookmarking alters inheritance.

candidates: ChIP/CUT&RUN of AP-1 (FOS/JUN) occupancy before, after, and long after transient stimulus
ATAC-seq time course tracking AP-1 motif accessibility after stimulus withdrawal
Acute degron (dTAG/AID) depletion of FOS/JUN after stimulus to test if memory maintenance requires AP-1
Degron depletion during stimulus only, to test requirement for memory establishment
Single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) lineage tracing of memory persistence across divisions
Optogenetic AP-1 activation pulses with varying dose/timing to test priming and memory decay
dCas9-KRAB/dCas9-p300 targeting of AP-1 sites to test sufficiency of the chromatin state
Mutating AP-1 motifs at a memory enhancer via base editing and assaying recall response
Live imaging of FOS/JUN reporter dynamics in single cells and correlating with later responsiveness
Mitotic bookmarking assay: AP-1 retention on mitotic chromosomes by live imaging/CUT&RUN
Dominant-negative A-FOS expression to block AP-1 and test loss of secondary response potentiation
Proteomics of AP-1 dimer composition shifts (FOS vs FOSL vs JUND) after stimulation
Co-occupancy analysis of AP-1 with BAF/SWI-SNF and pioneer factors via sequential ChIP
Histone mark (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) persistence at AP-1 sites after stimulus, with and without AP-1 depletion
Micro-C/Hi-C to detect persistent AP-1-dependent enhancer-promoter loops
Kinetic modeling of bistable feedback (FOS/JUN autoregulation) fitted to single-cell data
In vivo memory test: inflammatory training in mice, then sorted cells assayed for AP-1 occupancy and challenge response
Optical-tweezers/single-molecule residence time of AP-1 on nucleosomal DNA
Cross-cell-type comparison of AP-1 memory (epithelial stem cells, macrophages, neurons) using existing datasets
Perturb-seq screen of AP-1 family members and cofactors for effect on memory persistence
Methylation/CpG state at AP-1 sites after memory (bisulfite) to separate DNA methylation from AP-1
Inhibit DNA replication/cell cycle to test whether memory requires division-dependent propagation
